_comment: Performance budget, enforced by scripts/check-budget.mjs in CI.
Every limit is set from a real measurement of dist/ with roughly 15 to 20
percent headroom, so ordinary work does not trip it and a genuine
regression does. The measured values on the day it was written are in
'measured', which is what makes the headroom auditable rather than a
There is deliberately no --update flag. A budget you can raise by running
a command is a report, not a gate: the one time it matters is the time
somebody is in a hurry, and that is exactly when it would be raised.
Changing a limit is a commit, with a reason.

codeTransferKb.why: JS, CSS and HTML, gzipped, which is what the browser actually pulls over the wire. The number a heavy new dependency moves first.

fontsKb.why: Every font subset shipped. Woff2 is already compressed so raw size is transfer size. This over-counts what one visitor fetches, since a browser takes only the subsets its text needs, which makes it a safe ceiling rather than an estimate.

firstLoadKb.why: Code plus every font: the worst case a first visit can cost before any media loads. The number a person actually waits for, because MediaSlot lazy-loads video and images.

videoKb.why: All shipped video. Lazy-loaded, so it does not delay first paint, but it is two thirds of the repository's weight and the thing most likely to grow without anyone noticing.

imageKb.why: All shipped stills. Screenshots are WebP, encoded at the lowest quality clearing 40 dB PSNR, so a regression here usually means a PNG got committed by accident.

totalKb.why: Everything in dist/. A bandwidth and repository-weight metric, not a user-facing one; firstLoadKb is the user-facing one.

largestAssetKb.why: The biggest single file, currently media/p3.mp4. Catches one unoptimised export dropped in, which a total-size budget can absorb without complaining.
